Assume that periodic measures are dense among all shift-invariant probability measures on \(X\). Then \(X\) satisfies Typical Periodic Optimization in the Lipschitz category: the space of Lipschitz functions \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) contains an open dense subset whose every member has exactly one maximizing measure, supported on a single periodic orbit.

Suppose a Banach space \(X\) has a unique unconditional basis, in the sense that any two normalized unconditional bases of \(X\) are equivalent after a permutation. Prove that \(X\) is isomorphic to its Cartesian square \(X \oplus X\).

Consider the Hardy module \(H^2(\mathbb D^2)\) on the bidisk, viewed as a module over \(\mathbb C[z_1,z_2]\). For a nonconstant homogeneous polynomial \(p\) in the complex variables \(z_1,z_2\), write \([p]\) for the principal homogeneous submodule it generates. Then \(p\) is square-free exactly when the quotient module \(H^2(\mathbb D^2)/[p]\) is subnormal.

An approximate one-dimensional quantum cellular automaton (QCA) on a finite circle is an automorphism of the tensor product algebra of local quantum systems whose locality preservation is accurate up to a small error. Strict 1D QCAs admit a classification by one topological index, but the classification of approximate QCAs on a finite circle is richer. In particular, some approximate QCAs cannot be rounded to any strict QCA; the obstruction to such a rounding yields a secondary \(\mathbb{Z}_2\) topological index.

Fix a countable Turing ideal \(\Gamma\); that is, \(\Gamma\) is a nonempty countable collection of reals closed under Turing joins and downward closed under Turing reducibility. Call a map \(h:\mathbb{R}^{+}\to\mathbb{R}^{+}\) a gauge function when it is right-continuous and non-decreasing, with
\[
\lim_{x\to 0+}h(x)=0.
\]
For functions \(g\) and \(h\), eventual domination of \(h\) by \(g\) means that some \(\delta>0\) satisfies
\[
g(x)\ge h(x)\qquad\text{for every }x\in(0,\delta).
\]
Then, for any gauge function \(h\), the set of \(\Gamma\)-Mathias generics has positive Hausdorff measure with respect to \(h\) exactly when no gauge function \(g\in\Gamma\) eventually dominates \(h\).

Consider a bounded sequence \((c_n)_{n\ge 1}\) of complex numbers, and define \(f_c(z)=z^3+cz\). If the non-autonomous Julia set generated by \((f_{c_n})_{n\ge 1}\) is totally disconnected, then the non-autonomous dynamical system determined by this sequence is necessarily hyperbolic.

Suppose \(X\) is a compact Kähler manifold equipped with a nef and big class \(\alpha\), and let \(E\) be a holomorphic vector bundle on \(X\). Assume that, with respect to \(\alpha\), the bundle \(E\) is slope polystable and equality holds in the Bogomolov–Gieseker inequality. Then \(E\) is projectively flat everywhere on \(X\).

Consider the Toeplitz operator $T_f$ acting on the Bergman space $A^2(\mathbb{D})$ of the unit disk, where its symbol $f$ is bounded, radial, and real-valued. Denote the Berezin transform of $f$ by $\widetilde{f}$. The boundary condition
\[
\liminf_{|z|\to 1^-}\widetilde{f}(z)\ge 0
\]
implies that the essential spectrum of $T_f$ is contained in the nonnegative real axis:
\[
\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(T_f)\subset [0,\infty).
\]

On \(\mathbb{Z}^2\), consider the discrete Schrödinger operator
\[
H_V=\Delta+V,
\]
with \(\Delta\) the discrete Laplacian and \(V\) a real-valued potential periodic with respect to \(q_1\mathbb{Z}\oplus q_2\mathbb{Z}\). For each \(\lambda\in\mathbb{C}\), define \(F_\lambda(V)\) to be the set of quasimomenta \(k=(k_1,k_2)\in\mathbb{C}^2\) for which there is a nonzero function \(u\) satisfying
\[
H_Vu=\lambda u,
\qquad
u(n+q_je_j)=e^{2\pi i k_j}u(n),\quad j=1,2.
\]
Potentials \(V\) and \(W\) are called Fermi isospectral at \(\lambda\) when their Fermi varieties coincide:
\[
F_\lambda(V)=F_\lambda(W).
\]
Show that Fermi isospectrality with the zero potential at energy \(0\), namely
\[
F_0(V)=F_0(0),
\]
forces \(V\equiv 0\).

Suppose \(k\) is a field with \(\operatorname{char}(k)=p>0\), and let \(G\) be a finite abelian \(p\)-group whose minimal number of generators is even. Given any \(kG\)-module \(M\) expressible as a direct sum of syzygies and cosyzygies of the trivial module \(k\), set
\[
c_n=\dim_k\operatorname{core}\!\left(M^{\otimes n}\right),
\]
where the core denotes the non-projective part. Then \((c_n)\) is eventually recursive, or, equivalently, its formal generating function
\[
\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}c_nt^n
\]
is rational.

Suppose \(G\) is a \(2\)-connected graph with \(n\) vertices, where \(n\ge 4\) is an integer, and \(\delta(G)\ge \sqrt{n}\). Then for each integer \(k\) satisfying \(4\le k\le n\), there is a \(2\)-connected subgraph of \(G\) having exactly \(k\) vertices.

Let \(M\) be any closed surface. The space of \(C^1\) diffeomorphisms of \(M\) contains an open dense subset \(\mathcal{U}\) with the following property: every continuum-wise expansive diffeomorphism belonging to \(\mathcal{U}\) is Anosov.

For each integer \(\Delta \ge 3 \cdot 10^9\), a graph \(G\) can be found whose maximum degree is exactly \(\Delta\), whose clique number obeys \(\omega(G) \le \Delta - 1\), and whose correspondence chromatic number is \(\chi_{DP}(G) = \Delta\).

Let \(q,p\in\mathbb{R}^d\) denote the position and momentum of a particle governed by a non-Markovian generalized relativistic Langevin equation (GRLE), whose memory kernel is a finite sum of exponentials. Suppose its external potential \(U\in C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d;[1,\infty))\) obeys, for some \(a_1,a_2,a_3>0\) and \(\lambda\geq1\),
\[
\langle\nabla U(q),q\rangle\geq a_1|q|^{\lambda+1}-a_2,
\qquad
\frac{1}{a_3}|q|^{\lambda+1}-a_3
\leq U(q)\leq a_3\bigl(1+|q|^{\lambda+1}\bigr).
\]
Introducing auxiliary variables yields an equivalent Markovian system that is well-posed and geometrically ergodic: it has a unique Gibbs distribution and converges to that distribution exponentially fast in total variation distance.

Let \(F\) be any \(3\)-uniform hypergraph. Define \(r(F,n)\) to be the least integer \(N\) for which every \(F\)-free \(3\)-uniform hypergraph on \(N\) vertices contains an independent set of size \(n\). Then one of two alternatives holds: there is a polynomial \(p(n)\) such that \(r(F,n)\le p(n)\) for every \(n\), or there is a constant \(\delta>0\) such that \(r(F,n)\ge 2^{n^\delta}\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).

For a graph \(G\) with vertex set \(V\), consider labelings of its vertices by elements of \(\{0,1,2,3\}\). The weight of a labeling is the sum of its vertex labels.

A labeling \(f:V\to\{0,1,2,3\}\) is called a **double Roman dominating function** when it satisfies both of the following requirements:
- Every vertex labeled \(0\) has either at least two neighbors labeled \(2\) or at least one neighbor labeled \(3\).
- Every vertex labeled \(1\) has a neighbor labeled \(2\) or \(3\).

Write \(\gamma_{dR}(G)\) for the least possible weight \(\sum_{v\in V}f(v)\) of such a function.

A labeling \(g:V\to\{0,1,2,3\}\) is called a **double Italian dominating function** if each vertex \(u\) whose label belongs to \(\{0,1\}\) satisfies
\[
\sum_{v\in N[u]}g(v)\ge 3,
\]
where \(N[u]\) denotes the closed neighborhood of \(u\). Let \(\gamma_{dI}(G)\) be the minimum weight among all double Italian dominating functions on \(G\).

Prove that every tree \(T\) satisfies
\[
\gamma_{dI}(T)=\gamma_{dR}(T).
\]
For each integer \(d \ge 1\), every strongly irreducible subshift over \(\mathbb{Z}^d\) has a residually finite automorphism group.

Let \(S\) be the finite state space of a discrete-time imprecise Markov chain. Assume that its family of transition matrices is compact and convex, with separately specified rows, and fix a target set \(A \subset S\). Write \(\overline{h}(x)\) and \(\underline{h}(x)\) for the upper and lower expected times to hit \(A\) starting from \(x \in S\), and write \(\overline{p}(x)\) and \(\underline{p}(x)\) for the corresponding upper and lower probabilities of hitting \(A\). For every initial state \(x \in S\), the following equivalence holds:
\[
\underline{h}(x) < \infty
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\overline{p}(x) = 1.
\]

Write \(\mathrm{WKL}\) for weak Kőnig's lemma. Under Weihrauch reducibility, the Hahn–Banach theorem has degree \(\mathrm{WKL}\) when the Banach space is allowed to vary. In contrast, its restriction to the single Banach space \(\ell^1\) has Weihrauch degree strictly below that of \(\mathrm{WKL}\).
Consider the affine Grassmannian of an arbitrary simply-connected simple algebraic group \(G\). The Finkelberg–Mirković Schubert scheme corresponding to the quasi-minuscule coweight is reduced.

An entire graph \(S\) over the horosphere in the three-dimensional light cone \(\mathbb{Q}^3_+\) is necessarily a horosphere of \(\mathbb{Q}^3_+\), provided that its mean curvature is constant and its Gaussian curvature \(K\) is bounded from below.

Consider a measure-preserving dynamical system \((\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P},\sigma)\) and a measurable map \(f:\Omega\to\mathcal{H}\), where \(\mathcal{H}\) is the space of orientation-preserving homeomorphisms of \(\mathbb{S}^1=\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}\). The map \(f\) generates a discrete-time random dynamical system. Choose its standard random lift \(F\) by requiring that, for every \(\omega\in\Omega\), the lift \(F_\omega:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}\) of \(f_\omega\) obeys \(F_\omega(0)\in[0,1)\). Suppose also that
\[
\int_\Omega \|F_\omega-\mathrm{Id}\|\,d\mathbb{P}(\omega)<\infty.
\]
Prove that if some \(x\in\mathbb{S}^1\) satisfies \(f_\omega(x)=x\) for every \(\omega\in\Omega\), then the mean random rotation number
\[
\rho(F)=\int_\Omega \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{F_\omega^{(n)}(0)}{n}\,d\mathbb{P}(\omega)
\]
belongs to \(\mathbb{Z}\).

Consider the pentagram map \(P\) on planar polygons, obtained by taking intersections of diagonals to form a new polygon. Prove that any pentagon \(X\) for which
\[
P^2(X)\sim X,
\]
where \(\sim\) denotes equivalence under translation and scaling (homothety), is an affine image of a regular pentagon.

Define the Rank-$r$ Constrained Nonnegative Gram Feasibility problem by the following decision task. The input consists of an integer $n$, prescribed values for some entries of a symmetric matrix $W \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$, and a collection of affine constraints on its entries. Decide whether there is a nonnegative matrix $H \in \mathbb{R}_+^{n \times r}$ whose Gram matrix $HH^\top$ agrees with every prescribed entry of $W$ and satisfies every affine constraint.

For $r = 2$, this problem admits a polynomial-time algorithm; for each fixed integer $r \ge 3$, it is $\exists\mathbb{R}$-complete.

Suppose \(X\) is a connected, locally compact metric space, and consider a Markov chain \((Z_n)_{n\geq 0}\) taking values in \(X\). Its transition operator \(U\) is assumed to be Feller on the bounded continuous functions and is given by
\[
U\varphi(x)=\mathbb{E}\!\left[\varphi(Z_1(x))\mid Z_0=x\right].
\]
Call this chain an e-chain when, for each compactly supported continuous function \(\varphi\in C_c(X)\), the collection
\[
\{U^n\varphi:n\in\mathbb{N}\}
\]
is equicontinuous on every compact subset of \(X\).

Assume that \((Z_n)_{n\geq 0}\) is an e-chain and has exactly one stationary probability measure, denoted by \(\mu\). Show that it satisfies the strong law of large numbers: for every initial state \(x\in X\) and every \(\varphi\in C_c(X)\),
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^{n}\varphi(Z_k(x))
=\int_X\varphi\,d\mu
\qquad\text{almost surely}.
\]

Fix an integer \(N\) satisfying \(1 \le N \le 9\), and choose exponents \(1 \le p < q \le \infty\). Write \(B_1\) and \(B_{1/2}\) for the open balls in \(\mathbb{R}^N\), centered at the origin, of radii \(1\) and \(1/2\), respectively. For the equation
\[
-\Delta u=f(u)\qquad\text{in }B_1,
\]
a classical solution is said to be stable when
\[
\int_{B_1}\bigl(|\nabla \xi|^2-f'(u)\xi^2\bigr)\,dx\ge 0
\]
for every \(\xi\in C_0^1(\overline{B_1})\) that vanishes on \(\partial B_1\).

Show that one can choose a constant \(C>0\), depending exclusively on \(N,p,q\), so that for every \(f\in C^\infty(\mathbb{R})\) and every stable solution \(u\in C^\infty(\overline{B_1})\) of this equation, one has
\[
\|u\|_{L^q(B_{1/2})}\le C\,\|u\|_{L^p(B_1)}.
\]

Consider a finite, non-atomic measure space \((X,\Sigma,\mu)\) and exponents satisfying \(1\leq p<q<\infty\). For a measurable function \(u:X\to\mathbb C\) and a measurable, non-singular map \(\varphi:X\to X\), define the weighted composition operator by
\[
(Wf)(x)=u(x)f(\varphi(x)).
\]
There are choices of \(u\) and \(\varphi\) for which \(W:L^q(\mu)\to L^p(\mu)\) is both non-zero and nuclear.

Suppose \(F\in\mathcal{O}(\mathbb{C}^3)\) and the collection of entire functions
\[
\bigl\{z\mapsto F(z,a,b):(a,b)\in\mathbb{C}^2\bigr\}
\]
forms a normal family on \(\mathbb{C}\). Show that its dependence on \(a\) and \(b\) can be expressed through one entire parameter: there are entire maps \(\phi:\mathbb{C}^2\to\mathbb{C}\) and \(g:\mathbb{C}^2\to\mathbb{C}\) for which
\[
F(z,a,b)=g\bigl(z,\phi(a,b)\bigr)
\qquad\text{for every }(z,a,b)\in\mathbb{C}^3.
\]

A commutative association scheme admits a multivariate \(P\)- or \(Q\)-polynomial structure relative to an elimination-type monomial order precisely when it can be expressed as a direct product of univariate \(P\)- or \(Q\)-polynomial schemes.

Fix a prime power \(q\), a positive integer \(n\), and an integer \(d\) satisfying \(2 \le d \le n\). On the vertex set \(\mathbb{F}_q^n\), define \(\operatorname{Gilbert}(q,n,d)\) by joining distinct vectors whenever their Hamming distance is less than \(d\). Thus, in its complement \(\overline{\operatorname{Gilbert}(q,n,d)}\), adjacency means that the Hamming distance is at least \(d\).

Prove that \(\overline{\operatorname{Gilbert}(q,n,d)}\) is distance-transitive exactly when it is edge-transitive.

Suppose \(P\) consists of \(n\) points in the plane in convex position. Define \(F(P)\) to be the graph whose vertices represent the non-crossing spanning trees on \(P\), with two vertices adjacent precisely when one tree is obtained from the other by replacing a single edge. Given two such trees, their shortest-path distance in \(F(P)\) can be computed in polynomial time.

Suppose a Banach space \(X\) has a closed subspace \(M\) for which both \(M\) and the quotient \(X/M\) are isomorphic to the same Hilbert space \(H\); such an \(X\) is called a twisted Hilbert space. Show that \(X\) is isomorphic to its topological dual \(X^*\).

Suppose \(M\) is a smooth, closed manifold equipped with any choice of Morse function and Riemannian metric. Then \(M\) has the same homotopy type as the classifying space of the Morse flow category determined by these choices.

Let \(n \ge 2\) be an integer, and let \(X\) be a proper, geodesically complete CAT(0) space. If \(X\) is quasi-isometric to Euclidean space \(\mathbb{R}^n\), then \(X\) is homeomorphic to \(\mathbb{R}^n\).

The Farey graph has a pseudofinite first-order theory, with finite planar graphs providing the witnesses: for any finite collection of sentences from this theory, there is a finite planar graph in which all of those sentences hold.

For a countable group \(G\), consider sequences of approximate homomorphisms into matrices that converge strongly: for every polynomial in the group elements, the corresponding matrix norms converge to the norm obtained from the left regular representation. A group admitting such a sequence is called a **matricial field (MF) group**. If the maps in the sequence can all be taken to be genuine homomorphisms, \(G\) is called **purely MF (PMF)**. If, in addition, every one of these homomorphisms has finite image, \(G\) is called **purely finite field (PFF)**.

The fundamental group of every closed hyperbolic \(3\)-manifold is PMF. However, there are closed hyperbolic \(3\)-manifolds whose fundamental groups fail to be PFF.

Suppose \((M,g,X)\) is a complete expanding gradient Ricci soliton that is asymptotically conical. Show that if the tangent cone at infinity of \((M,g)\) is a Kähler cone, then \((M,g,X)\) is a Kähler-Ricci soliton.

For a graph \(G\), call an assignment \(L\) a \(k\)-assignment if it gives every vertex \(v\in V(G)\) a list \(L(v)\) containing exactly \(k\) colors. A sequence \((\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_k)\) is an \(L\)-packing when each \(\phi_i\) is a proper coloring of \(G\), each color \(\phi_i(v)\) belongs to \(L(v)\), and
\[
\{\phi_1(v),\ldots,\phi_k(v)\}=L(v)
\qquad\text{for every }v\in V(G).
\]
Define \(\chi_l^{\star}(G)\), the list packing number, to be the least integer \(k\) for which every \(k\)-assignment of \(G\) admits an \(L\)-packing. If \(t(d)\) denotes the maximum value of \(\chi_l^{\star}(G)\) over all graphs \(G\) with tree-width at most \(d\), prove that
\[
t(d)\le 2d-1
\qquad\text{for every integer }d\ge 2.
\]

Fix an integer \(n\ge 2\), and equip \(M_n(\mathbb C)\) with the operator norm \(\|\cdot\|\). For each linear subspace \(E\subseteq M_n(\mathbb C)\), define its structured singular value at \(A\in M_n(\mathbb C)\) by
\[
\mu_E(A)=\frac{1}{\inf\bigl\{\|X\|:X\in E,\ \det(I_n-AX)=0\bigr\}},
\]
with the convention that \(\mu_E(A)=0\) when no \(X\in E\) satisfies \(\det(I_n-AX)=0\).

Prove that a linear subspace \(F\subseteq M_n(\mathbb C)\) satisfying
\[
\mu_F(A)=\|A\|\qquad\text{for every }A\in M_n(\mathbb C)
\]
must be the whole space \(M_n(\mathbb C)\).

Let \(\Sigma\) be a complete Riemannian surface with no boundary. Then \(\Sigma\) admits a triangulation \(G\subset\Sigma\) for which the inclusion map
\[
G^{(1)}\hookrightarrow\Sigma
\]
is a quasi-isometry, where the simplicial \(1\)-skeleton \(G^{(1)}\) carries the path metric obtained by assigning length \(1\) to every edge.

Consider a rational arrival process (RAP) represented by finite real square matrices \(G_0,G_1\) and a real initial row vector \(\nu\). For every \(k\ge 1\) and every choice of \(t_1,\ldots,t_k\ge 0\), its joint density is
\[
f_k(t_1,\ldots,t_k)
=\nu e^{G_0t_1}G_1\cdots e^{G_0t_k}G_1\mathbf{1},
\]
with \(\mathbf{1}\) denoting the column vector whose entries are all one. Assume that these joint densities are strictly positive, that \(G_0\) has a unique dominant real eigenvalue, and that the exact normalisation condition
\[
(G_0+G_1)\mathbf{1}=\mathbf{0}
\]
holds, where \(\mathbf{0}\) denotes the zero column vector. Under these assumptions, there exists a finite-dimensional Markovian arrival process (MAP) equivalent to the RAP.

Suppose that \(K\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is a cone over a closed, strictly convex \(C^3\) manifold whose second fundamental form is non-degenerate. Then \(K\) is a quadric or is made up of pieces of quadrics if and only if the billiard dynamics in \(K\), viewed as a discrete-time Hamiltonian system, is completely integrable.

Suppose \((M,g)\) is a compact static three-manifold with \(\partial M\neq\varnothing\), and the vector space of static potentials on \(M\) has dimension at least two. Show that there is a static potential \(u\) on \(M\) such that
\[
u^{-1}(0)\neq\varnothing
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
u^{-1}(0)\cap\partial M=\varnothing.
\]

Let \(d>1\), and place the Ising model at its critical temperature on the Erdős–Rényi graph \(G(n,d/n)\), whose average degree is \(d\). For a spin configuration \(\sigma\in\{-1,1\}^n\), define the magnetization by
\[
M_n=\sum_{i=1}^n \sigma_i.
\]
As \(n\to\infty\), the quenched distribution of \(n^{-3/4}M_n\) converges in distribution, with respect to the \(1\)-Wasserstein distance induced by the Kolmogorov–Smirnov metric, to a deterministic probability measure. The limiting measure has density
\[
\frac{1}{Z}\exp(-Cz^4)
\]
for some constant \(C>0\).

Start with the root \(0\) and construct a random recursive tree by adding, at each time \(n \ge 1\), a vertex labelled \(n\) whose parent is chosen uniformly from \(\{0,\dots,n-1\}\). Along this growth process, perform Bernoulli bond percolation with a fixed parameter \(p \in (0,1]\), retaining each newly added edge with probability \(p\). Write \(P(p)\) for the probability that, at every time \(n\), the cluster containing the root is among the largest clusters. There is a threshold \(p_c \in (0,1)\) for which \(P(p)=0\) whenever \(p<p_c\), whereas \(P(p)>0\) whenever \(p>p_c\).
Any ribbon knot admits a presentation as a symmetric union.
A link \(L \subset S^3\) having at least two components is fibered if and only if the commutator subgroup \([G,G]\) of its link group \(G=\pi_1(S^3\setminus L)\) is finitely generated.

Suppose \(\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is an open, bounded, convex domain equipped with a smooth convex potential \(V\). For the Schrödinger operator \(-\Delta+V\) on \(\Omega\), let \(u\) denote its first Dirichlet eigenfunction, scaled so that \(\|u\|_\infty=1\). Show that
\[
x\longmapsto \sqrt{-\log u(x)}
\]
is convex throughout \(\Omega\); in other words, \(u\) is \(1/2\)-logconcave on \(\Omega\).

Fix an integer \(N \ge 3\), and suppose \(L \subset \mathbb{S}^3\) is a hyperbolic link with \(N\) components. Write
\[
X_L=\mathbb{S}^3\setminus \operatorname{int}(N(L)),
\]
where \(N(L)\) denotes a regular neighborhood of \(L\). Assume that \(P\subset X_L\) is an incompressible planar surface whose boundary meets each boundary torus of \(X_L\) in exactly one component, so that \(P\) is spanning. Then some component of \(\partial P\) has slope \(a/p\), measured in the standard meridian–longitude coordinates, with \(p\in\{0,1\}\); equivalently, at least one boundary slope is meridional or integral.

For each integer \(k \ge 3\), there exist a countable group \(G\), a finite symmetric generating set \(S\) for \(G\), a probability measure \(\mu\) whose support generates \(G\) as a semigroup, and a Borel probability measure \(\nu\) on the Chabauty space \(\operatorname{Sub}_G\) of subgroups of \(G\), with the following properties:

- The random subgroup \(\nu\) is \(\mu\)-stationary for the conjugation action \(g.H=gHg^{-1}\); that is,
  \[
  \nu=\sum_{g\in G}\mu(g)\,(g.\nu).
  \]
- For \(\nu\)-almost every \(H\in\operatorname{Sub}_G\), the Schreier graph determined by \(S\), whose vertices are the cosets in \(H\backslash G\) and whose edges are
  \[
  Hg\longrightarrow Hgs \qquad (s\in S),
  \]
  has exactly \(k\) ends.

Suppose \(X\) is a projective surface that is Kobayashi hyperbolic and carries a Hermitian metric of strictly negative holomorphic sectional curvature. Then the Kähler–Einstein metric on \(X\) necessarily has strictly negative holomorphic sectional curvature as well.

Construct a tree $\mathcal{T}$ rooted at $(0,0)$ as follows. Its backbone is the infinite path through the vertices $(i,0)$, $i\ge0$, in increasing order of $i$. At each $(i,0)$ with $i\ge1$, attach a trap consisting of the path
\[
(i,0),(i,1),\ldots,(i,i).
\]
Thus the vertex set is
\[
V=\{(i,j):i\ge0,\ 0\le j\le i\},
\]
and the only edges are
\[
\{(i,0),(i+1,0)\}\quad(i\ge0),
\qquad
\{(i,j-1),(i,j)\}\quad(i\ge1,\ 1\le j\le i).
\]

Fix $0<\lambda<1$ and let $(X_n)_{n\ge0}$ be the $\lambda$-biased random walk on this tree: at every vertex other than the root, assign weight $\lambda$ to the edge leading to its parent, the neighbor nearer the root, and weight $1$ to each edge leading to a child, then normalize these weights to obtain the transition probabilities. Writing $|X_n|$ for the distance of $X_n$ from the root, the walk obeys the almost-sure law of large numbers
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{|X_n|}{\log n}
=\frac{1}{\log(1/\lambda)}.
\]

Suppose \(G\) is a connected graph with \(n\) vertices and diameter \(2\). Write \(D(G)\) for its distance matrix, and define the transmission of a vertex \(v\) by
\[
\operatorname{Tr}_G(v)=\sum_{u\in V(G)}d_G(u,v).
\]
The distance Laplacian of \(G\) is
\[
D^L(G)=\operatorname{diag}\bigl(\operatorname{Tr}_G(v):v\in V(G)\bigr)-D(G).
\]
Order its eigenvalues as
\[
\partial_1^L(G)\ge \partial_2^L(G)\ge\cdots\ge \partial_n^L(G),
\]
and set
\[
W(G)=\sum_{\{u,v\}\subseteq V(G)}d_G(u,v),
\]
the Wiener index. Show that, for every integer \(r\) with \(1\le r\le n\),
\[
\sum_{i=1}^{r}\partial_i^L(G)\le W(G)+\binom{r+2}{3}.
\]

Call a linearly ordered structure weakly o-minimal if each definable subset of its domain can be expressed as a finite union of convex sets. Suppose that \(\mathcal{M}=(M,+,\cdot,\le,\dots)\) is an expansion of an ordered field with this property. Prove that, given any definable open set \(U\subseteq M\) and any definable map \(f:U\to M\), one can find an open interval \(I\subseteq U\) such that \(f\) is differentiable on \(I\).

For a graph \(G\), write \(\lambda(G)\) for the largest eigenvalue of its adjacency matrix, that is, its spectral radius. Given \(1<p\le 2\), associate to each graph \(G\) on \(n\) vertices the quantity
\[
d_p(G)=\max_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq V(G)}
\frac{e(G[S])}{|S|^p},
\]
where \(G[S]\) is the subgraph induced by \(S\) and \(e(G[S])\) counts its edges. Show that there is a positive constant \(C_p\), depending on \(p\) alone, for which every \(n\)-vertex graph \(G\) containing at least one edge obeys
\[
\lambda(G)\le (C_p+o(1))\,d_p(G)\,n^{\max\{1/2,p-1\}}
\qquad\text{as }n\to\infty.
\]

For a finite set \(X\), say that a map \(f\colon X^k\to X\) admits an embedding into a polynomial of total degree \(d\) over a commutative ring \(R\) when one can choose an injective map \(j\colon X\to R\) and a polynomial \(g\in R[x_1,\ldots,x_k]\) with total degree at most \(d\) satisfying
\[
g\bigl(j(v_1),\ldots,j(v_k)\bigr)
=
j\bigl(f(v_1,\ldots,v_k)\bigr)
\qquad\text{for every }(v_1,\ldots,v_k)\in X^k.
\]

There is an integer \(d\ge 1\), independent of both \(X\) and \(f\), for which every binary map \(f\colon X^2\to X\) on every finite set \(X\) admits such a polynomial embedding of total degree at most \(d\) over a suitable commutative ring \(R\).

Suppose that \(K\) is a number field and that \(X\) is a homogeneous space under \(\mathrm{SL}_n\) over \(K\), whose geometric stabilizers are finite and nilpotent. Assume that \(X(K_v)\neq\varnothing\) for every completion \(K_v\) of \(K\), and that the unramified algebraic Brauer group of \(X\) consists entirely of constant classes; explicitly,
\[
\ker\!\left(\mathrm{Br}_{\mathrm{nr}}(X)\longrightarrow
\mathrm{Br}_{\mathrm{nr}}(X_{\bar K})\right)
=
\mathrm{im}\!\left(\mathrm{Br}(K)\longrightarrow\mathrm{Br}(X)\right).
\]
These hypotheses imply that \(X(K)\neq\varnothing\).

Write \(\mathrm{ex}(n,F)\) for the largest number of edges possible in an \(F\)-free graph on \(n\) vertices. Define \(h_F(n,q)\) to be the smallest number of subgraphs isomorphic to \(F\) among all \(n\)-vertex graphs having \(\mathrm{ex}(n,F)+q\) edges. Also define \(c(n,F)\) as the least number of such copies obtainable by inserting a single edge into an extremal \(F\)-free graph on \(n\) vertices. Whenever \(F\) has at least one cycle, the equality
\[
h_F(n,1)=c(n,F)
\]
holds for every sufficiently large integer \(n\).

Equip the real torus \(\mathbb{R}^n/\mathbb{Z}^n\) with a positive definite quadratic form on \(\mathbb{R}^n\), and denote the resulting tropical abelian variety by \(\mathcal{A}\). Suppose that \(X\subseteq\mathcal{A}\) is a pure \(d\)-dimensional tropical subvariety: that is, a weighted, embedded, rational polyhedral \(d\)-complex whose slopes are integral and which satisfies the balancing condition. The topological Euler characteristic of \(X\) then satisfies
\[
(-1)^d\chi(X)\geq 0.
\]

Let \(p\) be a prime and let \(T\) be an algebraic torus defined over \(\mathbb{Q}\). Writing \(T(\mathbb{Z}_p)\) for the maximal compact subgroup of \(T(\mathbb{Q}_p)\), one has
\[
T(\mathbb{Q}_p)=T(\mathbb{Z}_p)T(\mathbb{Q}).
\]

Consider structures with two sorts: a point set \(X\) and a linearly ordered distance set \(D_X\) whose least element is \(0\). Such a structure is called a two-sorted ultrametric space when it is equipped with a symmetric function \(d:X\times X\to D_X\) satisfying, for all \(x,y,z\in X\),
\[
d(x,y)=0 \iff x=y,
\qquad
d(x,z)\leq \max\{d(x,y),d(y,z)\}.
\]
For two such spaces \(X\) and \(Y\), a dc-embedding is a pair of injections
\[
f:X\to Y,\qquad D_f:D_X\to D_Y,
\]
where \(D_f\) preserves the order and \(0\), and
\[
d_Y(f(x),f(y))=D_f(d_X(x,y))
\quad\text{for every }x,y\in X.
\]

Take \(\mathbb{U}\) to be the Fraïssé limit of the class of all finite two-sorted ultrametric spaces, using dc-embeddings. Prove that \(\operatorname{Aut}(\mathbb{U})\) has ample generics: for each integer \(n\geq 1\), the group \(\operatorname{Aut}(\mathbb{U})^n\) has a comeager conjugacy class.

Suppose that \((X,\mathcal{E})\) is a uniformly locally finite coarse space. For each \(p\in\{0\}\cup[1,\infty]\), define the \(\ell^p\) uniform Roe algebra \(B^p_u(X,\mathcal{E})\) to be the norm closure of \(\mathbb{C}_u[X,\mathcal{E}]\), the algebra of controlled propagation operators acting on \(\ell^p(X)\). Call a closed two-sided ideal \(I\subseteq B^p_u(X,\mathcal{E})\) geometric when \(I\cap\mathbb{C}_u[X,\mathcal{E}]\) is dense in \(I\).

Given \(p,q\in(1,\infty)\), the geometric-ideal lattices of \(B^p_u(X,\mathcal{E})\) and \(B^q_u(X,\mathcal{E})\) are isomorphic exactly when either \(p=q\) or
\[
\frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{q}=1.
\]

Suppose \(G\) is a simple, connected, undirected graph having \(n\) vertices and \(m\) edges. If \(\lambda_2(G)\) is the second-largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix of \(G\), then
\[
\lambda_2(G)\leq \sqrt{m-\frac{n}{2}-\frac{1}{2}}.
\]

Suppose that \(E\) is a \(\mathrm{W}^*\)-bundle over a compact Hausdorff space \(X\) of covering dimension zero. If there is a \(\mathrm{II}_1\) factor to which every fibre of \(E\) is isomorphic, then \(E\) is locally trivial.

Suppose \((M,g)\) is a complete, noncompact Riemannian manifold of dimension \(n\) whose Ricci curvature is nonnegative. Prove that \((M,g)\) is isometric to Euclidean space \(\mathbb{R}^n\) whenever the equation
\[
-\Delta_n u=e^u \quad \text{on }M
\]
admits a weak solution
\[
u\in W^{1,n}_{\mathrm{loc}}(M)\cap L^\infty_{\mathrm{loc}}(M).
\]
Here the weak solution condition means that, for every compactly supported \(\varphi\in W^{1,n}_0(M)\),
\[
\int_M |\nabla u|^{n-2}g(\nabla u,\nabla\varphi)\,dV_g
=
\int_M e^u\varphi\,dV_g.
\]

Fix a prime \(p>0\) and a homomorphism \(f:R\to S\) between commutative rings of characteristic \(p\). Call \(f\) **b-nil formally unramified** when the following uniqueness property holds: whenever \(A\) is a ring of characteristic \(p\) and \(I\subset A\) is an ideal for which the ideal generated by \(\{a^p:a\in I\}\) vanishes, each \(R\)-algebra map \(S\to A/I\) admits at most one lift \(S\to A\) as an \(R\)-algebra map.

Regard \(R\) as an \(R\)-algebra through its absolute Frobenius \(x\mapsto x^p\), and denote this algebra by \(F_*R\). The relative Frobenius associated to \(f\) is
\[
F_{S/R}:F_*R\otimes_R S\longrightarrow F_*S,
\qquad r\otimes s\longmapsto rs^p.
\]

Show that \(f\) is formally unramified precisely when \(F_{S/R}\) is an epimorphism in the category of rings.

For a commutative ring \(R\) with identity, write \(Z(R)\) for its set of zero-divisors and define
\[
\operatorname{ann}_R(x)=\{r\in R\mid rx=0\}.
\]
Construct the inclusion graph of annihilators \(\Gamma^{\prime}(R)\) by taking \(Z(R)^*=Z(R)\setminus\{0\}\) as its vertex set and joining distinct vertices \(x\) and \(y\) precisely when their annihilators are comparable under inclusion; that is,
\[
\operatorname{ann}_R(x)\subseteq\operatorname{ann}_R(y)
\quad\text{or}\quad
\operatorname{ann}_R(y)\subseteq\operatorname{ann}_R(x).
\]
Prove that \(\Gamma^{\prime}(R)\) is disconnected if and only if \(R\) is isomorphic to a direct product of two integral domains.
Show that an acylindrically hyperbolic group \(G\) has uniform exponential growth whenever it satisfies Kazhdan's property \((T)\).

A closed manifold \(M\) is called **of Jiang-type** when every continuous self-map \(f\colon M\to M\) has Nielsen, Lefschetz, and Reidemeister numbers satisfying
\[
L(f)=0 \implies N(f)=0,
\qquad
L(f)\ne 0 \implies N(f)=R(f).
\]
For a group \(G\), **property \(R_{\infty}\)** means that each automorphism \(\varphi\in\operatorname{Aut}(G)\) gives rise to infinitely many \(\varphi\)-twisted conjugacy classes, where the equivalence relation is
\[
\alpha\sim \sigma\alpha\varphi(\sigma)^{-1},
\qquad \alpha,\sigma\in G.
\]
Whenever \(M\) is of Jiang-type and \(\pi_1(M)\) possesses property \(R_{\infty}\), it follows that \(M\) is aspherical.

Let \(N=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) index the players in a mixed-integer linear-quadratic generalized Nash equilibrium problem (MI-LQ-GNEP). For each \(i\in N\), the player’s decision is determined by
\[
\begin{aligned}
\min_{x_i}\quad & \sum_{j\in N}x_j^\top Q_{ij}x_i+d_i^\top x_i\\
\text{subject to}\quad & \sum_{j\in N}A_{ij}x_j\ge b_i,\\
& x_i\in\mathbb{R}_+^{l_i}\times\mathbb{Z}_+^{k_i}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Suppose that every entry of \(Q_{ij}\), \(A_{ij}\), \(d_i\), and \(b_i\) is rational. Within this class, the existence of a Nash equilibrium guarantees the existence of a rational equilibrium if and only if every player’s objective has no quadratic term in that player’s own variables, namely,
\[
Q_{ii}=0\qquad\text{for all }i\in N.
\]

An irreducible Coxeter group \(W\) is finite if and only if, for every fixed integer \(k \ge 0\), its Bruhat intervals of length \(k\) fall into finitely many isomorphism classes. Here the length of an interval \([u,v]\) is \(\ell(v)-\ell(u)\), where \(\ell\) denotes the length function on \(W\).

There are an amenable unimodular random rooted network of finite expected degree, a finite-range operator \(D\), and a value \(\lambda \in \mathbb{C}\) such that the \(\lambda\)-eigenspace of \(D\) has strictly positive von Neumann dimension, whereas, almost surely, every \(\lambda\)-eigenfunction of \(D\) on the network has infinite support.

Fix \(q\) with \(0<q<1\). Set
\[
(q;q)_0=1,\qquad
(q;q)_k=\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}(1-q^{j+1})\quad(k\ge1),
\]
so that \((q;q)_k\) is the \(q\)-Pochhammer symbol. On formal power series, introduce the normalized \(q\)-Borel operator by
\[
\mathcal{B}_q\!\left(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}a_k\frac{z^k}{k!}\right)
=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}
\frac{a_kq^{k(k-1)/2}(1-q)^k}{(q;q)_k}\,z^k.
\]
Write \(\mathcal{L-P}\) for the classical Laguerre--Pólya class of real entire functions. The restriction of \(\mathcal{B}_q\) to \(\mathcal{L-P}\) is a bijection for every \(q\in(0,1)\); that is, \(\mathcal{B}_q\) maps \(\mathcal{L-P}\) surjectively onto itself.

Write \(\mathrm{Ga}(\alpha,\beta)\) for the Gamma law whose density is
\[
p(z;\alpha,\beta)
=\frac{z^{\alpha-1}}{\beta^\alpha\Gamma(\alpha)}
\exp(-z/\beta),\qquad z>0.
\]
An observation \(x\sim\mathrm{Ga}(\alpha,\beta)\) is available for predicting an independent random variable \(y\sim\mathrm{Ga}(T\alpha,\beta)\). Here \(\alpha>0\) and \(T>0\) are fixed and known, whereas the scale \(\beta>0\) is unknown. For Kullback–Leibler loss, the Bayesian predictive density obtained from the Jeffreys prior \(\pi(\beta)\propto 1/\beta\) is admissible exactly when \(\alpha>1\).

A lattice polytope is called Ehrhart positive when its Ehrhart polynomial has no negative coefficients. Suppose that \(P \subset \mathbb{R}^p\) and \(Q \subset \mathbb{R}^q\) are lattice polytopes, and define their join by
\[
P * Q
=
\operatorname{conv}\!\left(
\{(x,0_q,1):x\in P\}
\cup
\{(0_p,y,0):y\in Q\}
\right)
\subset \mathbb{R}^{p+q+1}.
\]
Ehrhart positivity of both \(P\) and \(Q\) always implies Ehrhart positivity of \(P * Q\).

Fix a prime \(p\) and a positive integer \(n\), and take a cyclic group \(G\) of order \(p^n\). For any subgroup \(H\leq \operatorname{Aut}(G)\), write \(\mathcal{S}(G,H)\) for the orbit Schur ring over \(G\) whose basic sets are the \(H\)-orbits. Then the association scheme corresponding to \(\mathcal{S}(G,H)\) has an almost commutative Terwilliger algebra exactly when either \(H=\{1\}\) or \(H=\operatorname{Aut}(G)\).

For an integer \(d\ge 2\), choose \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\) and let \(1<p<\infty\). Define the discrete Riesz transform \(R_{\mathrm{dis}}^{(k)}\) on \(\ell^p(\mathbb Z^d)\) as the convolution operator whose kernel is
\[
K_k(m)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle c_d\,\frac{m_k}{|m|^{d+1}}, & m\in\mathbb Z^d\setminus\{0\},\\[6pt]
0, & m=0,
\end{cases}
\qquad
c_d=\frac{\Gamma\!\left(\frac{d+1}{2}\right)}{\pi^{(d+1)/2}}.
\]
The norms of these operators admit a dimension-independent bound: there is a constant \(C_p>0\), depending on \(p\) alone, for which
\[
\bigl\|R_{\mathrm{dis}}^{(k)}\bigr\|_{\ell^p(\mathbb Z^d)\to\ell^p(\mathbb Z^d)}
\le C_p
\]
for every \(d\ge 2\) and every \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\).

Fix \(d \ge 2\) and \(H \in (1/4,1/2]\). On the canonical path space
\[
\Omega=\{\omega\in C([0,1],\mathbb{R}^d):\omega_0=0\},
\]
equipped with its Borel \(\sigma\)-algebra and Gaussian measure, let \(X\) be a \(d\)-dimensional fractional Brownian motion of Hurst parameter \(H\). Choose \(\eta\in(0,H)\) satisfying
\[
\frac1\eta<\left\lfloor\frac1H\right\rfloor+1.
\]

Consider random variables
\[
\mathbf X:\Omega\longrightarrow
C^{\eta\text{-Höl}}\!\left([0,1],
\mathcal G^{\lfloor1/H\rfloor}(\mathbb R^d)\right)
\]
whose first level is \(X\). Such a lift is called local if, whenever \(0\le s\le t\le1\), \(n\le\lfloor1/H\rfloor\), and \(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), its component \(\mathbf X_{s,t}^{\alpha_1\cdots\alpha_n}\) is measurable with respect to
\[
\sigma\!\left(
X_u^\alpha-X_s^\alpha:
u\in[s,t],\ 
\alpha\in\{\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n\}
\right).
\]
Call the lift square-integrable when all its components belong to \(L^2(\Omega)\).

Restrict attention to local, square-integrable \(\eta\)-Hölder rough path lifts that obey the following distributional symmetries:
\[
\mathbf X_{s,t}\sim\mathbf X_{0,t-s},
\qquad
\mathbf X_{s,t}^{(n)}
\sim(t-s)^{nH}\mathbf X_{0,1}^{(n)},
\qquad
\sigma_*\mathbf X\sim\mathbf X
\quad\text{for every }\sigma\in\mathfrak S_d.
\]
These express invariance in law under time translation, scaling, and permutation of coordinates, respectively. For every \(H\in(1/4,1/2]\), the canonical lift is the only lift in this class.

For a finite group \(G\), write \(k(G)\) for its number of conjugacy classes. Show that
\[
k(G)\leq \max\bigl\{|N|:N\leq G \text{ and } N \text{ is nilpotent}\bigr\}.
\]

In the siblings version of coupon collection, an independent sequence of coupons is sampled from \(N\) types, with type \(i\) appearing with probability \(p_i\), where \(\mathbf{p}=(p_1,\ldots,p_N)\) lies in the probability simplex. The collectors are arranged in order: collector \(1\) keeps the first coupon of each type and forwards every duplicate to collector \(2\). Each subsequent collector follows the same rule, keeping any type not yet in their collection and passing all other coupons to the next collector.

Sampling ends when collector \(1\) first possesses all \(N\) types. Write \(U_j^N(\mathbf{p})\) for the number of types absent from collector \(j\)'s collection at that moment. For every pair of integers \(N\ge 2\) and \(j\ge 2\), show that
\[
\mathbf{p}\longmapsto \mathbb{E}\!\left[U_j^N(\mathbf{p})\right]
\]
is Schur-concave on the probability simplex, and hence is maximized by the uniform probability vector
\[
\mathbf{p}=\left(\frac1N,\ldots,\frac1N\right).
\]

A graph \(G\) is called \(H\)-saturated when it contains no subgraph isomorphic to \(H\), yet inserting an edge between any pair of non-adjacent vertices creates such a subgraph. Write \(\mathrm{sat}(n,H)\) for the least number of edges among all \(H\)-saturated graphs with \(n\) vertices. Use \(K_m^-\) for the complete graph \(K_m\) with one edge removed, and \(K_1\vee F\) for the graph formed from \(F\) by adjoining a new vertex adjacent to every vertex of \(F\).

For each integer \(p\ge 4\), set \(F=K_{p-1}^-\cup K_1\). Then, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
\mathrm{sat}(n,K_1\vee F)=n-1+\mathrm{sat}(n-1,F).
\]

Consider a convex polygon \(\mathcal P\) in the plane whose vertices, in cyclic order, are \(P_1,\ldots,P_{2n}\). Interpret all subscripts modulo \(2n\), and write \(e_i=P_{i+1}-P_i\). Assume that, for every \(i\),
\[
e_i\parallel e_{i+n}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\langle e_i,e_{i+1}\rangle>0.
\]
Denote its perimeter and enclosed area by \(L(\mathcal P)\) and \(A(\mathcal P)\), respectively. The Wigner caustic \(\mathrm E_{0.5}(\mathcal P)\) is the polygon formed by the vertices
\[
W_i=\frac{P_i+P_{i+n}}2,
\]
and its oriented area is defined by
\[
A^\ast\bigl(\mathrm E_{0.5}(\mathcal P)\bigr)
=\frac12\sum_{i=1}^{2n}\det(W_i,W_{i+1}).
\]

Prove that
\[
L(\mathcal P)^2\geqslant
8n\tan\left(\frac{\pi}{2n}\right)
\left(A(\mathcal P)+2\left|A^\ast\bigl(\mathrm E_{0.5}(\mathcal P)\bigr)\right|\right),
\]
and that equality occurs precisely when \(\mathcal P\) is a regular \(2n\)-gon.

Equip the set of lines in \(\mathbb{R}^d\) with the quotient topology induced by
\[
\{(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{R}^d:x\ne y\},
\]
where two pairs are identified precisely when they determine the same line. Show that, for each integer \(d\geq 1\), if \(\mathcal{F}\) is a finite collection of at least two mutually disjoint open convex subsets of \(\mathbb{R}^d\), then every connected component of the space of lines meeting every member of \(\mathcal{F}\) is acyclic; that is, its reduced homology is trivial.

Fix an integer \(d\ge 3\). For every sufficiently large integer \(n\), any family \(\mathcal F\) of \((d+1)\)-element subsets of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\) whose VC-dimension equals \(d\) satisfies
\[
|\mathcal F|\le \binom{n-1}{d}+\binom{n-4}{d-2}.
\]

There is a positive rational number \(r\) that can be represented by the convergent series
\[
r=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} a_n2^{-a_n},
\]
where the terms \(a_n\) are positive integers satisfying
\[
a_1<a_2<\cdots
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{a_n}{n}=\infty.
\]

Suppose \(R\) is an integral domain, and write \(R^\times\) for its group of units. Use the following terminology:

- A nonzero nonunit \(a\in R\) is called an **atom**, or **irreducible**, when every decomposition \(a=bc\) has at least one of \(b,c\) in \(R^\times\).
- An element of \(R\) is **atomic** when it is either a unit or a finite product of atoms. If all nonzero elements of \(R\) are atomic, call \(R\) an **atomic domain**.
- The **irreducible divisor finite (IDF) property** means that, for each nonzero element of \(R\), its atom divisors represent only finitely many associate classes.
- Call \(R\) **nearly atomic** when some nonzero \(s\in R\) has the property that every nonzero member of \(sR\) is atomic in \(R\).
- Call \(R\) **almost atomic** when every nonzero \(r\in R\) admits an atomic element \(s\in R\) for which \(rs\) is atomic in \(R\).
- A **finite factorization domain (FFD)** is a domain in which each nonzero nonunit admits a factorization into atoms and has only finitely many such factorizations, with permutations of factors and replacement by associates disregarded.

Show that \(R\) is an FFD precisely when \(R\) is almost atomic and has the IDF property.

Fix an integer \(N\ge 1\) and parameters satisfying
\[
0<s<1,\qquad p>1,\qquad 0\le\gamma<\min\{2s,N,2s(p-1)\}.
\]
Choose a nonnegative, nonzero function
\[
u_0\in L^1(\mathbb{R}^N)\cap L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^N).
\]
For initial amplitude \(\varepsilon>0\), write \(T_\varepsilon\in(0,\infty]\) for the lifespan of mild solutions of
\[
\begin{cases}
u_t+(-\Delta)^s u=|x|^{-\gamma}|u|^p,
& (t,x)\in(0,\infty)\times\mathbb{R}^N,\\
u(0,x)=\varepsilon u_0(x),
& x\in\mathbb{R}^N.
\end{cases}
\]
Here the fractional Laplacian is given by
\[
(-\Delta)^s f(x)
=c_{N,s}\,\operatorname{P.V.}\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}
\frac{f(x)-f(y)}{|x-y|^{N+2s}}\,dy,
\qquad
c_{N,s}
=\frac{2^{2s}\Gamma\!\left(\frac{N+2s}{2}\right)}
{\pi^{N/2}|\Gamma(-s)|}.
\]
Set
\[
p_F=1+\frac{2s-\gamma}{N}.
\]
There is a number \(\varepsilon_0>0\) for which every \(0<\varepsilon<\varepsilon_0\) satisfies the following lifespan dichotomy:
\[
T_\varepsilon<\infty\quad\text{when }1<p<p_F,
\qquad
T_\varepsilon=+\infty\quad\text{when }p\ge p_F.
\]

Consider a connected bipartite graph embedded in a closed orientable surface; such an embedding is called a dessin d'enfant. Its passport records, as three partitions of its number of edges, the degrees of the black vertices, the white vertices, and the faces, in that order. The passport is said to be uniform if all parts within each of these three partitions are equal. Every uniform passport of genus at least \(2\) is realized by a dessin d'enfant whose automorphism group is trivial.

Fix positive integers \(n\) and \(k\) satisfying \(k\le n\), and consider collecting \(n\) distinct coupons by receiving \(k\) distinct coupons on each draw. A mechanism selects uniformly from a prescribed family of \(k\)-element subsets of the coupon set. Call the mechanism fair when each coupon belongs to the same number of members of that family.

Write \(T_{\mathcal M}(n,k)\) for the expected number of independent draws required to obtain every coupon using a fair mechanism \(\mathcal M\). Write \(T_{\mathrm{full}}(n,k)\) for the corresponding expectation when each of the \(\binom{n}{k}\) possible subsets is equally likely.

Show that, for every such \(n,k\) and every fair mechanism \(\mathcal M\),
\[
T_{\mathcal M}(n,k)\le T_{\mathrm{full}}(n,k).
\]

Consider a stiffness tensor
\[
\mathbf{a}\in \operatorname{Sym}^2_+\bigl(\operatorname{Sym}^2(\mathbb{R}^2)\bigr),
\]
where this space consists of positive definite quadratic forms on the symmetric tensor square of \(\mathbb{R}^2\). Associate to each \(\xi\in\mathbb{R}^2\) the Christoffel matrix whose entries are
\[
\bigl(\Gamma_{\mathbf{a}}(\xi)\bigr)_{ij}
=\sum_{k,l}a_{iklj}\xi_k\xi_l.
\]
Define the slowness polynomial and its planar zero locus by
\[
P_{\mathbf{a}}(\xi)=\det\bigl(\Gamma_{\mathbf{a}}(\xi)-I\bigr),
\qquad
\Sigma_{\mathbf{a}}=\{\xi\in\mathbb{R}^2:P_{\mathbf{a}}(\xi)=0\}.
\]
The algebraic curve \(\Sigma_{\mathbf{a}}\), called the planar slowness surface, admits precisely the following singularity types: ordinary nodes, meaning transverse self-intersections; ordinary tacnodes, meaning tangential singularities arising where a concentric circle and ellipse touch; and ordinary cusps.

Suppose that \(E_1\) and \(E_2\) are definable equivalence relations in a simple first-order theory \(T\). Assume that each is stable and satisfies the non-finite cover property (NFCP). Prove that the relational composition \(E_1 \circ E_2\) is stable.

Suppose \(q\ge 2\) is an integer and \(F\) is a graph for which \(q\mid e(F)\). Define \(R(F,\mathbb Z_q)\) to be the smallest integer \(n\) with the following property: for every assignment \(w\colon E(K_n)\to\mathbb Z_q\), there is a subgraph isomorphic to \(F\) whose edge labels add to zero in \(\mathbb Z_q\).

Write \(K_{s,t}\) for the complete bipartite graph with part sizes \(s\) and \(t\). For every \(s\ge 2\) and \(k\ge 1\), the zero-sum Ramsey number is given by
\[
R(K_{s,3k},\mathbb Z_3)=
\begin{cases}
s+3k+1, & \text{if }s=2,\text{ or if }k=1\text{ and }s\in\{3,4,5,6,7\},\\
s+3k, & \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]

Equip \(\mathbb{R}^3\) with the Lorentzian metric
\[
\langle\, , \,\rangle=-(dx^0)^2+(dx^1)^2+(dx^2)^2,
\]
and write \(\mathbb{L}^3\) for the resulting Lorentz–Minkowski space. Given an open Riemann surface \(M\), a smooth map \(X:M\to\mathbb{L}^3\) is termed a maxface when its differential is nowhere zero and some open dense set \(W_X\subset M\) has the property that \(X|_{W_X}\) is a space-like immersion whose mean curvature vanishes identically. Define the singular set \(S\subset M\) to consist of precisely those points at which the induced metric \(\langle dX,dX\rangle\) is degenerate.

Show that, for every open Riemann surface \(M\) and every maxface \(X:M\to\mathbb{L}^3\), the set \(X(S)\) is nowhere dense in \(\mathbb{L}^3\).

Suppose \(B=(B,+,\circ)\) is a finite skew brace, and associate to each \(a\in B\) the map
\[
\lambda_a(b)=-a+a\circ b.
\]
An additive subgroup of \(B\) is called a left ideal if it is invariant under every \(\lambda_a\). A subset of \(B\) is called a sub-skew brace if it forms a subgroup under each of the operations \(+\) and \(\circ\).

Fix a prime \(p\). A Sylow \(p\)-sub-skew brace of \(B\) means a sub-skew brace whose order equals the largest power of \(p\) dividing \(|B|\). Prove that any sub-skew brace of \(B\) having \(p\)-power order lies in a Sylow \(p\)-sub-skew brace of \(B\).

Write \(P_4\) for the path with \(4\) vertices. For a graph \(G\), consider the smallest number of colors in an edge-coloring of \(G\) in which each copy of \(P_4\) has all its edges colored differently. Define \(\chi_{\mathrm{S}}(n,e,P_4)\) to be the minimum of this number as \(G\) ranges over all graphs with \(n\) vertices and exactly \(e\) edges.

Prove that, given any \(\epsilon>0\), one can choose a constant \(c(\epsilon)>0\) such that, for every sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
\chi_{\mathrm{S}}\left(n,\binom{n}{2}-\lfloor n^{2-\epsilon}\rfloor,P_4\right)>c(\epsilon)n^2.
\]

A closed manifold is said to virtually fibre over the circle when it has a finite covering \(M' \to M\) whose total space \(M'\) fibres over the circle. Suppose that \(M\) is closed and aspherical, with dimension \(d \ge 3\), and that \(\pi_1(M)\) is residually (torsion-free and nilpotent). If all the \(L^2\)-Betti numbers of \(M\) vanish over every field, then \(M\) virtually fibres over the circle.

Let \(d\ge 2\), and consider the incompressible Navier–Stokes equations in \(\mathbb{R}^d\) for a one-phase free boundary flow with surface tension, whose initial fluid region lies outside a bubble. Viscosity and surface tension together provide enough regularization to rule out finite-time splash singularities. More precisely, if the bubble collapses in finite time—meaning that its free boundary intersects itself—then the supremum of the principal curvatures of that boundary must blow up as the collapse time is approached.

Let \(N \ge 3\) and \(\alpha > 0\). A non-radial, positive classical solution of the critical Hénon equation
\[
-\Delta u = |x|^\alpha u^{\frac{N+2+2\alpha}{N-2}}
\qquad \text{in } \mathbb{R}^N
\]
with Newtonian-type decay
\[
u(x)=O\!\left(|x|^{2-N}\right)
\qquad \text{as } |x|\to\infty
\]
exists precisely when \(\alpha=2(k-1)\) for some integer \(k\ge 1\).
